core_obligations: Quasi-compact case (proof lines 7348-7366): when X and all X_i are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the objects of the two sites are compared using the standard description of affine etale schemes over the limit as base changes of affine etale schemes over some X_i, which identifies the site with the colimit.

General case (proof lines 7369-7394): for an arbitrary object U of X_{affine, etale}, the author writes U as an etale separated scheme over X and descends it to a stage of the system, using that affine transition morphisms make the relevant base changes affine, which gives the identification in general.
Both paragraphs also verify the compatibility of the topologies, since the coverings on both sides are detected by the same affine etale coverings.
proof_roadmap: Assume first that the schemes are quasi-compact and quasi-separated and identify objects by descent along the affine transition morphisms.
In general, descend an arbitrary affine etale object to some stage of the inverse system.
Check that coverings correspond, which gives the equality of sites in the sense of the colimit construction.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the affine etale site of a directed limit of schemes with affine transition morphisms is the colimit of the affine etale sites of the approximants (statement lines 7335-7346). The proof treats two cases: the quasi-compact quasi-separated case, where objects and coverings are compared directly through the standard description of affine etale objects over a limit as base changes over some stage (proof lines 7348-7366), and the general case, where an arbitrary affine etale object over the limit is descended to some stage using affineness of the transition morphisms (proof lines 7369-7394). The non-formal content is the descent of objects and coverings to a stage, and the verification that the topologies correspond. The claim is H2: two cases, both written out.
